newsitem.title: IRAQ: Pro-Saddam Kurds, rivals clash at key Iraqi town.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Saddam Kurds, rivals clash at key Iraqi town.

text.p: Pro-Baghdad Iraqi Kurdish militiamen launched a counter-attack on Tuesday to take back a key town from a rival guerrilla group pushing through northern Iraq, witnesses said.

Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) fighters deployed near the town of Degala fired heavy machineguns towards Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) positions in a bid to recapture the nearby town of Koy Sanjak.
"We will get back Koy Sanjak by ascending hill-by-hill," Arif Tayfur, regional commander of KDP forces, told Reuters.
Hundreds of his fighters were taken to the front in two armoured personnel carriers and a fleet of battered buses and cars.
But witnesses, who said the attack began around 9:00 a.m. local time (0500 GMT), reported no sign of any Iraqi or Iranian forces taking part or supporting the Kurdish combatants.
Jalal Talabani's PUK has won back much of the ground it lost last month to KDP forces backed by Iraqi troops and tanks. The PUK took back Koy Sanjak, Talabani's home town, several days ago.
Massoud Barzani's KDP has accused its rival of receiving Iranian military aid. Tehran denies this.

KDP commander Tayfur said Iranian forces and the Bedr militia, a pro-Tehran Iraqi Shiite group, had pulled back towards the Iranian border after helping Talabani capture the city of Sulaimaniya at the weekend.
"We started our attack because the Iranian troops and Badr fighters were pulled back to the region between Sulaimaniya and the Iran border," he said.
"We have enough forces to push back the PUK forces in Koy Sanjak." He said he expected to take the town within a day.
